page.layout: One column of text on a single printed page. Running head at the top, page number 202 at the top left. Above the text a large block of quoted law in capitals, then a small italic subheading, then the body paragraph in a single column. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: ” DECEM MENSIBVS PROXIMIS, QVIBVS FILIVS MEVS MORERETVR, NATVS NATA ERIT, HAEREDES SVNTO. Quidam rectè admittè-dum credunt, etiam si nō exprimat de morte filij, sed simpliciter instituat: ut eo casu ualeat, qui ex uerbis concipi posit[?]. ”
main_text.head: Interpretatio Grammatica.
main_text.p: GAllus sic posse.) Hic est C. Aquilius Gallus, Iurisc. auditor Q. Mutij Sceuolę, & Ser. Sulpitij praeceptor, ut constat ex L. 2. de orig. iur. & Cicero-ne in Bruto. Magnus formularum cō-cipiendarum artifex, unde illa de dolo malo nobilis, quam Cicero euerriculum malitiarum omnium appellat: item illa Aquiliana acceptilatio, de qua in Pandectis frequentissime. page.notes: Running head at the top is set in heavy bold type and cannot be read reliably. The first letters of the body paragraph are a large woodcut-style initial G joined to "Allus". The quoted law at the top is set in capitals, and each line begins with a printed quotation mark. "posit[?]" is a doubtful reading: the scan shows "posfit", with the long s rendered as a plain s. The page ends mid-word with the hyphen printed on "Iurisconsul-" and continues on the next page. Short line breaks in "Cicero-ne" and "cō-cipiendarum" are printed hyphens.
